# Codex wire contract reference

`raine-contract.json` contains six synthetic requests and outputs generated by
running the actual `raine/claude-code-proxy` translator and header builder at
`fe107180f7a69c6d63dd4421a6567cf641c1f103` (main verified 2026-11-12).

Generator entrypoints:

- `providers::codex::translate::request::translate_request`
- `providers::codex::client::build_codex_headers`

Cases cover Lite/full lanes, medium/high effort, an in-history system message,
function-tool regex schemas with literal data to preserve, and structured output.
All credentials/content in this file are synthetic (`mock-*`, `synthetic *`).
No live account or network inference was used to produce the expected values.

The tests compare complete JSON payloads. Full-lane `originator` and `user-agent`
are normalized to this application's name/version; Lite headers are compared
unchanged. The compiled reference translator is not a runtime/build dependency.
Fixture regeneration is optional; normal tests use this checked-in snapshot.
To regenerate, clone the pinned revision into a temporary directory and copy
`export_contract.rs` into its `examples/` directory as `llm_proxy_export_contract.rs`.
Create the input JSON by extracting each fixture's name/model/lite/input fields,
then run the example in that clone with `cargo run --locked --example
llm_proxy_export_contract < cases.json > regenerated.json`. The helper constructs
mock StoredAuth directly; it does not load token stores or make inference calls.

The schema walkers in `src/adapters/outbound/codex/schema.rs` are ported from that same
revision, rather than independently reimplemented. Removing pattern constraints
relaxes tool argument validation, matching the reference's native compatibility
policy; literal defaults/examples/property names are preserved.

Reference: https://github.com/raine/claude-code-proxy/tree/fe107180f7a69c6d63dd4421a6567cf641c1f103
MIT attribution is retained in the repository's `LICENSE`.
